1Purpose

This policy is the frame for every specialist disability accommodation (SDA) matter at [Provider name]. It names the four thread policies that carry our commitments, and the few rules that bind all of them. It protects the 's rights, their home and their choice of .

2Applies to

  • [Provider name] as a registered NDIS provider of SDA, whether SDA is our only class of supports or one of several.
  • Every we own, lease or manage for SDA, and every dwelling we apply to enrol. This covers every participant who lives in one or is offered a place. A prospective participant has the same rights as a participant (Practice Standards Rules, Schedule 7, clause 1(2)).
  • Everyone who works at or for a dwelling: employees, contractors, tradespeople, agents and volunteers.
  • A participant who provides SDA to themselves. The agreement rule in POL-SDA-03 does not apply to them (SDA Conditions Rule, section 9(3)). The dwelling rules do.
  • Our own supported independent living in an SDA dwelling. POL-SIL-05, POL-SIL-02, POL-SIL-03 and POL-SUP-03 apply as well.
  • Our two roles, as landlord and as support provider to the same participant. Every commitment applies to both.

3Commitments

Each commitment below points to the thread policy that carries it. The thread policy's numbers, roles and records are the only source of truth; this policy restates none of them.

C1

We will do what POL-SDA-02 Rights and Responsibilities Policy (Specialist Disability Accommodation) commits to: each participant's rights at home, their privacy, and every request to change their dwelling.

C2

We will do what the provider's of Interest Policy (POL-GOV-02) commits to, applied to SDA through PRO-SDA-03 Conflict of Interest Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation): every interest we hold is declared, and a participant's home never depends on their choice of supports.

C3

We will do what POL-SDA-03 Service Agreements with Participants Policy (Specialist Disability Accommodation) commits to: a written agreement with every participant, in the terms the law requires.

C4

We will do what POL-SDA-04 Enrolment of SDA Properties Policy commits to: kept within their enrolment, lawful, safe and in good repair.

C5

We will do what POL-SDA-05 Tenancy Management Policy (Specialist Disability Accommodation) commits to: fair vacancies, documented with each , and that follow the law.

4Ground rules

The thread policies carry their own ground rules. These four are the ones no thread policy carries, and they bind every SDA procedure.

G1

Every participant has a private bedroom unless they freely choose to share one (SDA Rules 2020, section 24(1)(d)). A participant who chooses to share must tell the in writing, and the NDIA must be satisfied that their needs are not harmed; a notice alone is not the end of it. We help them do it (SDA Rules 2020, section 24(1)(e)).

G2

Where we own or manage the dwelling, we lead on the dwelling, its repairs and its vacancies. A SIL provider leads on the supports it delivers. Where a matter involves both, the arrangement under AGR-SDA-02 SDA and Supported Independent Living Arrangements Agreement names one lead, and both act together.

G3

In a small provider one person may hold several roles. A sole trader names an for in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register, with a written delegation that covers every task the thread policies and procedures give that person. The independent contact is not a relative or business associate of the sole trader, has access to REG-SDA-01 SDA Dwelling Register, REG-SDA-02 SDA Tenancy and Vacancy Register and the register (REG-GOV-02), and is briefed on PRO-SDA-03 and PRO-SDA-04 Service Agreements with Participants Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation) before acting.

G4

If we will miss a time we promised a participant, we tell them before it passes, with the reason and the new date. A time the law sets cannot be moved.

9Words we use

567 words
SDA agreement
the written agreement between us and a participant about their home.
dwelling
a home in which we provide SDA. An enrolled dwelling is one the NDIA has enrolled so that SDA can be provided in it.
participant
a person with disability who lives in a dwelling, or is offered a place in one.
tenant
a person who lives in a dwelling and has a right to be there.
eligible participant
a participant the NDIA has decided is eligible for SDA funding (SDA Rules 2020, section 11).
other supports
every NDIS support a participant gets apart from the home, from us or from anyone else. Examples are SIL, support coordination and plan management.
supported independent living (SIL)
help with, or supervision of, daily tasks so a person can live as independently as possible.
design category and building type
the features the NDIA enrolled a dwelling under. The SDA Rules 2020 set five design categories and four building types.
density limit
a cap on how many eligible participants can be funded for SDA across every dwelling on one parcel of land (SDA Rules 2020, section 31).
conflict of interest
a clash between what we, a worker or someone close to us gains and what is best for the participant. It is actual when it affects a decision, potential when it could, and perceived when it looks as if it could.
security of tenure
a participant's right to keep living in their home unless the SDA agreement and tenancy law allow it to end.
tenancy law
the law of [state or territory] about renting a home, including notices, bonds and entry.
notice to vacate
a written notice that tells a participant they must leave their home.
tenancy action
a notice to vacate, a breach notice, any rent or board increase, a room move, or a change to the agreement or house rules for one participant.
tenure check
the Chief Executive's decision, before a tenancy action is served, on whether anything links it to the participant's support decisions or worries.
modification
a change to the building, or to something fixed to it. An adjustment is a change to how we manage the dwelling, give notice or communicate.
urgent defect
a fault that puts anyone at risk of harm, or stops a participant washing, using the toilet, preparing food, sleeping or leaving home. Examples: no water or power, a gas or electrical fault, a broken lock or door, a failed lift, hoist or fire alarm, a blocked exit.
independent advocate
a person who is not part of [Provider name], chosen by the participant, who speaks up for their wishes and rights. An advocate does not make decisions for them.
independent contact
in a small provider, a person outside our management, named in REG-GOV-01, who acts when the Chief Executive has an interest.
NDIA
the National Disability Insurance Agency. The SDA Rules 2020 give its notices to its CEO.
NDIS Commission
the NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commission.
SDA Manager
the Service Manager for our SDA dwellings.
Tenancy Officer
the worker the SDA Manager assigns tenancy tasks to. In a small provider this is the SDA Manager.
business day
a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the state or territory where the participant lives.
SDA Rules 2020, SDA Conditions Rule, Practice Standards Rules, Complaints Rules, Incident Rules, Quality Indicators
short names for the instruments in Authority.

docs.html:
1Purpose

The result: every we enrol meets the requirements the enrolled it on. It stays within them. It is safe, secure, private and in good repair.

This procedure gives effect to POL-SDA-04 Enrolment of SDA Properties Policy, C1 to C14.

2When and who

Start this procedure when any of these happens:

  • we think about enrolling a dwelling
  • a person is offered a home in an
  • an inspection, a certificate or a service falls due
  • a worker, a , the owner or another provider reports a defect
  • something happens that the NDIA must be told about, or the NDIA writes to us
  • the check of the list of laws falls due every 12 months, or the law changes; or the report to the governing body falls due every 3 months
  • the sample re-inspection falls due every 12 months.

Who acts:

  • The opens each dwelling record, checks the dwelling, applies to the NDIA, inspects, rates and chases repairs, and tells the NDIA. The SDA Manager is the Service Manager for our SDA dwellings.
  • The is the worker the SDA Manager assigns tenancy tasks to. They tell residents, give notice of entry and warn the SDA Manager of each planned move-in. In a small provider the SDA Manager is the Tenancy Officer.
  • The Quality Manager checks the evidence before a certification, reviews the laws, re-inspects a sample and reports to the governing body.
  • The Chief Executive signs each certification to the NDIA, answers NDIA notices and decides when an enrolment may end.
  • Every worker reports each defect the same day.
  • The on-call manager makes an safe after hours.

In a small provider one person may hold several of these roles. A sole trader holds them all. A sole trader names an for in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register. That person checks the evidence at step 11 before the sole trader signs at step 12. They do the sample at step 29 and hear any concern about the sole trader. Where a step says to tell the next role, a sole trader writes down the time and carries on.

3Before you start

The SDA Manager:

  • You can open REG-SDA-01 SDA Dwelling Register and FRM-SDA-03 SDA Dwelling Inspection and Compliance Checklist.
  • You hold the current NDIS Pricing for Specialist Disability Accommodation (the SDA Rules 2020 still call it the SDA Price Guide) and the current SDA Design Standard, and you know their versions and dates: [Pricing Arrangements version and date]; [SDA Design Standard edition].
  • You have the list of laws for the dwelling's state or territory from REG-QMS-03 Compliance Obligations Register.
  • You have access to the my NDIS provider portal (myID and RAM), where enrolment applications are lodged, and you know the NDIA contact for SDA enrolment: [NDIA contact for SDA].

Everyone who acts:

  • You have each resident's FRM-RGT-01 Communication, Advocacy and Support Preferences Form, so you know how they want to be told things.
  • You know the repairs number, [repairs number], and the on-call number, [on-call number].
  • Workers: you know that any defect goes to the SDA Manager the same day (step 20).

4Watch out

  • If anyone is in danger, call 000 first. A gas smell, smoke, a fire alarm going off, live wiring or flooding near power can kill. The defect report comes second.
  • Providing SDA in a dwelling the NDIA has not enrolled breaks a condition of our registration. It can bring a civil penalty (SDA Conditions Rule, section 6(a); NDIS Act 2013, section 73J). Nobody moves in as an SDA resident until the enrolment is on the row.
  • A signed certification must be true. Applying for a dwelling that does not meet the requirements also breaks that condition. The NDIA can cancel an enrolment after a notice of at least 14 days (SDA Rules 2020, section 27).
  • The density count includes other people's dwellings. A count of our own dwellings alone can leave a parcel over its limit, and our dwelling out of its enrolment.
  • The NDIA clock starts on the event, not on the day we find the paperwork. A late notice breaks a condition of enrolment (SDA Rules 2020, section 29). The NDIA can cancel an enrolment for that.
  • A required design feature that stays out of use can change the dwelling's category. Residents lose the access the home was enrolled to give them. Fix it, and decide at once whether the NDIA must be told.
  • A lock, gate or sensor that limits a resident's movement may be a . Fit none without the authorisation the law requires. PRO-BSP-02 Regulated Restrictive Practices Procedure applies.
  • Entering a resident's home without lawful notice breaks and the resident's privacy. It also costs their trust in us.
  • A repair is never a reason to move a resident, or to change their supports. Housing and supports stay separate.

5Steps

Before we apply to enrol a dwelling

Step 1

The SDA Manager

Open a dwelling row for each dwelling we think about enrolling.

Give it a dwelling code. Write the address and the owner. Note the resident number of anyone who lives there now or may move in. A dwelling we manage but have not enrolled also gets a row. Nothing else starts until the row is open.

Result
The dwelling has a code, and its status is "being assessed".
Record
FRM-SDA-03 Q1 and Q7. REG-SDA-01 col A, col B, col R and col N
Time limit
Within 1 of deciding to assess a dwelling (our standard)
Step 2

Warning. We cannot certify the application without the owner's written agreement.

The SDA Manager

If we do not own the dwelling:

Get the owner's signed agreement.

It must say we may enrol the dwelling. It must also say the owner will not enrol it separately. A spoken yes is not enough. Check the owner's name against the land title. File the agreement.

Result
The owner's agreement is on file, and the dwelling row names the owner.
Record
FRM-SDA-03 Q8. REG-SDA-01 col S
Time limit
Before the application is lodged (statutory: SDA Rules 2020, section 25(4)(j))
Step 3

The Tenancy Officer

If anyone lives in the dwelling now, or has been offered a home there:

Tell each of them we plan to enrol the dwelling, and ask what they think.

Use the format each person chose in FRM-RGT-01. Say what enrolment means. The dwelling must keep to its category. The number of residents is capped. We tell the NDIA about certain changes. Say that it never changes their tenancy or their supports. Offer an advocate. Their words go on their own file. Use resident numbers only in the register.

Result
Each person knows about the application and has been heard before we apply.
Record
FRM-SDA-03 Q6
Time limit
Before the application is lodged (our standard)
Step 4

The SDA Manager

Match the dwelling to one SDA building type, using Decision table 1.

Walk the dwelling and the land. Check each feature in the table. Read Schedule 1 of the SDA Rules 2020 in full if the dwelling is close to two types. A dwelling that fits no type is not ready to enrol. File the Building Code class from its certificate of occupancy, or the equivalent. Photograph the outside, with no people in the photo.

Result
One building type is chosen, and its Building Code class agrees with the certificate.
Record
FRM-SDA-03 Q9. REG-SDA-01 col T
Time limit
Before the application is lodged (our standard)
Step 5

The SDA Manager

Decide whether the dwelling is a new build, existing stock or legacy stock, using Decision table 2.

Get the date the certificate of occupancy, or its equivalent, was first issued. Get the date of any renovation certificate. For existing or legacy stock, get the evidence about the earlier resident that the rule asks for. Read sections 6 to 8 of the SDA Rules 2020 in full before you decide. If the dwelling fits no class, stop and take advice.

Result
One stock class is chosen, and the evidence is on file.
Record
FRM-SDA-03 Q10. REG-SDA-01 col U
Time limit
Before the application is lodged (our standard)
Step 6

The SDA Manager

Fix the design category with the certification the dwelling's stock class requires.

For a new build, engage an accredited SDA assessor from the NDIA's list for design-stage and final as-built certification against the SDA Design Standard. The assessor must not be an employee, associate or contractor of us, the builder, the developer or the owner. The NDIA enrols a new build only on the final as-built certificate. For existing or legacy stock, engage an assessor who is not the builder and not on our staff to assess the shared areas, one bedroom and one bathroom against the Minimum Design Requirements for existing and legacy stock in the current NDIS Pricing Arrangements for Specialist Disability Accommodation. File the certificate or report, the SDA Design Standard edition or the Pricing Arrangements version it was assessed against, and the certificate reference. With consent, ask each which category their plan names.

Result
The category is fixed in writing by the right certification for the stock class, and the design standard it was assessed against is on file.
Record
FRM-SDA-03 Q11 and Q12. REG-SDA-01 col V and col W
Time limit
Before the application is lodged (our standard)
Step 7

The SDA Manager

Set the maximum number of residents and of eligible participants.

Count the bedrooms. Each eligible participant needs a private bedroom. A villa, duplex or townhouse is enrolled for 3 residents or fewer. A group home has 4 or 5 long-term residents. Do not count support staff. Set the number the layout can house safely, not the most the rules allow. Ask whether a provides SDA to themselves in this dwelling.

Result
Both maximums are set, and they fit the building type and the number of bedrooms.
Record

A signed certification is on file, or a recorded decision not to apply.

Within 5 business days of the Quality Manager's check (our standard)

The NDIA has the application, and we hold proof.

REG-SDA-01 col AE, col BI and col BJ

Within 5 business days of the Chief Executive's signature (our standard)

If the NDIA asks for more information or documents:

Send the NDIA what it asked for.

The NDIA has a full answer by its date.

REG-SDA-01 col BI, col BJ, col BK and col L

By the date in the NDIA's notice (statutory: SDA Rules 2020, section 25(5))

The row shows the decision, and nobody has moved in before enrolment.

REG-SDA-01 col AE, col BI, col BK and col N

The same day the decision arrives (our standard)

Check that a move-in keeps the dwelling inside its enrolled numbers and its .

The register shows the move-in is within the limits before it is confirmed.

REG-SDA-01 col AF, col AG, col AH and col M

Before the move-in is confirmed to the person (statutory: SDA Conditions Rule, section 11(a), and SDA Rules 2020, section 31)

The SDA Manager

Keep every certificate, approval and service in date.

Each item on the dwelling's list has its own row with a due date. Examples are safety alarm tests, lift and hoist services, hot water checks, backup power tests, pest treatment, and cleaning of gutters and drains. Result
No certificate or service on the list is past its date.

REG-SDA-01 col AI, col AJ, col AK, col L and col M

Renewal booked 30 days before the due date (our standard)
Step 18

The Tenancy Officer

Give each resident notice of the visit, in the format they chose, and agree a time.

Give the notice the tenancy law of [state or territory] requires for that reason, from the dated list of laws, and never less than our standard: 7 days for an inspection, 2 business days for a repair the resident asked for, and no notice in an emergency the law allows. Where the law requires more, the law applies. A resident may agree to less. Write down that they agreed. Say who is coming, why, when and which rooms. Ask which rooms they agree to and who they want there. Offer another time if they ask. A resident may say no to a room. Write it down. Each resident knows who is coming and when, and has agreed.

FRM-SDA-03 Q5 and Q6. REG-SDA-01 col BH

The longer of the notice the tenancy law of [state or territory] requires and 7 days for an inspection; 2 business days for a repair the resident asked for; no notice in an emergency the law allows (statutory for the law's period; our standard for the 7 days and 2 business days)

The SDA Manager

Inspect the whole dwelling with the residents, and complete FRM-SDA-03.

Walk each room the residents agreed to. Complete every Section. Compare what you see with the NDIA's enrolment confirmation, not only with our row. Every 6 months, or as often as the tenancy law of [state or territory] allows, if fewer. Within 5 business days of a change, an incident or an NDIA request. Residents told the result within 5 business days of the inspection (our standard)

Report, repair and close a defect

Step 20

Any worker who sees or hears of a defect

Report the defect to the SDA Manager the same day.

If anyone is in danger, call 000 first. A defect is anything broken, unsafe, leaking, missing or not working in the dwelling. A resident may tell any worker, in any way. A worker from another provider phones the repairs number. Phone the on-call manager at once for an emergency or an urgent defect. Emergency means a failure of power, backup power, water, a hoist, a call system or a way in and out for a resident whose support plan says they depend on it for breathing, feeding, suction, pressure care, medication or calling for help: call 000 if they are in danger, then the on-call manager at once, and the participant's medical emergency plan applies. Urgent means a fire or smoke alarm fault, exposed wiring, a gas smell, a door or window that cannot be locked, or no water or power. It also means a feature a resident relies on that is not working. Complete questions 1 to 4 and question 40 of FRM-SDA-03. Repair nothing yourself unless it is safe and you are trained.

Result
The SDA Manager knows about the defect and who reported it.
Record
FRM-SDA-03 Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4 and Q40
Time limit
Phone straight away for an emergency or urgent defect. Written report the same day (our standard)
Step 21

The SDA Manager

Rate each defect using Decision table 5, and act on its rating.

Acknowledge the report to the resident by the next business day, and say who will deal with it. Add a repair row for each defect. For an emergency defect, act the same hour: call 000 if anyone is in danger, apply the participant's medical emergency plan, and arrange interim power, equipment or a safe place with the and the participant's practitioner, who decide the clinical steps; make the home safe the same day. For an urgent defect, make the home safe within 24 hours, or arrange another safe way for the resident to use their room, bathroom or way in. After hours the on-call manager does this. A defect that stops a resident using a feature their design category needs is never routine. Tell each affected resident the rating, what we will do and by when, in the format they chose. Where a resident stays at risk until the fix, offer a choice of interim measures. Never ask a resident to move out.

Result
Each defect has a rating, an owner and a due date, and each affected resident knows.
Record
FRM-SDA-03 Q40 and Q44. REG-SDA-01 col AU, col AV, col AW, col K and col L
Time limit
Acknowledge by the next business day. Rate within 1 business day of the report, and the same day for an emergency or urgent defect. Make an emergency defect safe the same day and an urgent defect within 24 hours (our standard)
Step 22

The SDA Manager

Arrange the repair, and keep chasing it until it is done.

The duty to keep the dwelling in good repair stays with us even when the owner must do the work (SDA Rules 2020, section 28). Where the owner must act, send a written repair request the same day, and copy the resident with their consent. If the owner has not acted by the due date, arrange the work ourselves within 5 business days, or ask the Chief Executive to decide. We pay for repairs and upkeep that the law puts on us. Support a resident who wants to use their tenancy rights. The Tenancy Officer gives notice of entry under step 18 and adds an entry record.

Result
The work is booked with a date, and the person who does it and the person who pays are on record.

REG-SDA-01 col AX, col AY, col BH and col L

By the due date in Decision table 5. Where the tenancy law of [state or territory] gives a shorter time for an urgent repair, that time applies (our standard, and statutory where shorter)

The contractor is licensed, insured and briefed.

Before the contractor's first visit for each job (our standard)

The repair is checked, the resident has said it is fixed, and the row is closed.

Within 5 business days of the work being done (our standard)

Acknowledge it within 1 business day. Read it for its date and its conditions. The NDIA's request is answered in time, and each resident has been told.

Ask the participant's practitioner or an occupational therapist whether the dwelling stays suitable for each affected resident while the feature is out of use, and what interim measure is safe for them

Decision table 6: events the NDIA must be told about (step 25). The list is in section 29(1) of the SDA Rules 2020. The limit for every event is 5 business days (section 29(2)). Events (a) to (d) are notified under step 25 of this procedure. Events (e) to (g) are notified under PRO-SDA-05 Tenancy Management Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation) step 2, which owns them and uses this table for what to send.

7If it goes wrong

IfThen
A resident says no to the inspection, or to a roomRespect it. Explain again what the inspection is for, and offer another time or a supporter. Write "not inspected" and the reason at question 6. Ask the resident or their supporter to test the smoke alarm and tell us. Never enter without lawful notice and agreement
A resident does not answer the notice, or is awayTry 3 times on different days, in the way they chose, and ask their supporter. Write each attempt in the entry record. After 3 attempts, tell the Chief Executive. The Chief Executive decides whether to use the lawful entry ground for a safety inspection under the tenancy law of [state or territory], with the full statutory notice, or to ask the tribunal; the attempts in the entry record show the auditor why. For an urgent defect, use the entry rules in the tenancy law of [state or territory]

The owner will not agree, will not answer, or will not fix a defectWithout the owner's agreement, do not apply to enrol. For a defect, write to the owner, copy the resident, and fix it ourselves after the due date, as step 22 says. Support a resident who wants to use their tenancy rights, or an advocate
A deadline will be missed: a repair, a certificate or an NDIA dateThe owner of the action tells the SDA Manager before the date passes. For an NDIA date, the Chief Executive asks the NDIA in writing for more time. For a repair, keep the interim measure in place and tell the resident the reason and the new date. Record both. A new date for an urgent defect needs the Chief Executive's approval
We find that something we certified was wrong, or that the dwelling never met its category or typeTell the Chief Executive the same day. The Chief Executive takes advice and tells the NDIA in writing within 5 business days (POL-SDA-04, ground rule 6)
More people live in the dwelling than it is enrolled forTell the Chief Executive the same day. Admit no one else. Never ask a resident to leave except by a lawful process. The Chief Executive takes advice, and tells the NDIA and the in writing within 5 business days (our standard)
The NDIA refuses an enrolment, or cancels oneThe Chief Executive decides the next step the same day. Tell each resident in their format, and offer an advocate. Their tenancy stays under tenancy law, and PRO-SDA-05 Tenancy Management Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation) covers any notice. Ask for a review where the law allows
A design feature fails and cannot be back in use within 10 business daysGo to step 25 the same day. Keep an interim measure in place until it is back. Tell each resident the new date

Help each resident reach safe shelter of their choice. Complete an incident report under PRO-INC-01 Incident Management Procedure. A resident is hurt by a defectFollow PRO-INC-01 Incident Management Procedure. The Quality Manager decides whether the incident is reportable and notifies the NDIS Commission. Write the incident number at col P. Rate the defect urgent, or emergency where Decision table 5 says so
A resident complains about a defect, or about how we handled itFollow PRO-FBK-01 Feedback and Complaints Management Procedure. Keep the repair going. Nobody is treated worse for complaining

Where one is already there, the SDA Manager checks whether an authorised behaviour support plan covers it. If none does, the Chief Executive decides what to do the same day, with advice
A worker or contractor entered without notice, photographed a person, or damaged a resident's propertyTell the SDA Manager the same day. The SDA Manager tells the resident, offers to put it right and records an incident. A concern about abuse or exploitation follows PRO-SGD-01 Violence, Abuse, Neglect, Exploitation and Discrimination Procedure
The concern is about the SDA Manager, for example a defect marked fixed when it is notTell the Chief Executive. If it is about the Chief Executive or a sole trader, tell the independent contact for concerns. You may also tell the NDIS Commission on 1800 035 544. POL-GOV-03 Whistleblower and Disclosure Protection Policy protects you
The owner sells the dwelling or ends our leaseTell the Chief Executive the same day. Residents keep their tenancy rights under the law. A new owner must give the written agreement in step 2 before we can keep the dwelling enrolled. The Chief Executive decides whether event (b) or (d) in Decision table 6 applies
An eligible participant wants to share a bedroomIt is their free choice. Help them tell the NDIA in writing (SDA Rules 2020, section 24(1)(e)). Tell them that funding for the room depends on the NDIA agreeing that their needs are not adversely affected (section 24(1)(e)(ii)). Where the participant has a decision maker, take advice on who may make the choice before anything is sent. Write the date at col AG. Do not suggest it
The dwelling was enrolled before the SDA Rules 2020 startedThe law treats it as enrolled by the NDIA (SDA Rules 2020, section 41). Do not apply again. Open the dwelling row from the enrolment record you hold. Check its facts with steps 4 to 10 and step 19. Ask the NDIA to confirm the enrolled details in writing
The dwelling's feature list, certificate list or enrolment confirmation is missingDo not inspect from memory. Write "not known" with the date. Ask the NDIA in writing to confirm the enrolled details. Take the feature list from the design standard the dwelling was certified against: the SDA Design Standard edition on the assessor's certificate for a new build, or the Minimum Design Requirements in the NDIS Pricing Arrangements for Specialist Disability Accommodation for existing or legacy stock. Ask the owner for each certificate. Build the lists, and set a date to finish them
A resident dies, or leaves without noticeFollow PRO-INC-01 Incident Management Procedure first. Then use events (e) and (f) in Decision table 6. Section 32 of the SDA Rules 2020 names a participant who dies, and needs the NDIA to be told of the vacancy. Do not enter or clear the room until tenancy law allows it and the family or the executor has been told
The system is downUse the paper form and the paper log. The SDA Manager enters the rows within 1 business day of the system coming back

8Done means

An enrolled dwelling is ready for residents when all of these are true:

  • the NDIA has enrolled it, and its row shows the NDIA's reference
  • its building type, stock class, design category, bedrooms and enrolled maximums match the NDIA's confirmation
  • every matter we certified has evidence on file
  • its numbers and its density limit were checked before each move-in.

An enrolled dwelling stays compliant when all of these are true:

  • its last inspection and its last limits check are inside 6 months
  • every certificate and service on its list is in date
  • every defect has a rating, an owner and a due date
  • no emergency defect has gone past the same day, and no urgent defect past 24 hours, without being made safe
  • no other defect is past its Decision table 5 time, or past 14 days, without the resident's agreement
  • each event the NDIA must be told about was told inside the limit
  • every worker and contractor who works there has been briefed.

These records now exist:

  • the dwelling row, with its certified matters, application and the NDIA's decision, in REG-SDA-01
  • the completed FRM-SDA-03 for each inspection, with a row for each limits check, defect and entry
  • the certificate or service rows, each with its next due date
  • an NDIA matter row, with proof of sending, for each notice and answer
  • the briefing entries in REG-HRM-02 Training and Competency Register and REG-HRM-03 Contractor and Supplier Register
  • the report every 3 months, with its actions in REG-QMS-01 Continuous Improvement Register.

9Quick card

145 words
  • If anyone is in danger, call 000 first, then report every defect the same day (step 20)
  • Never provide SDA in a dwelling the NDIA has not enrolled (step 15)
  • Check numbers and the density limit before anyone moves in (step 16)
  • Make an emergency defect safe the same day, and an urgent defect within 24 hours (step 21)
  • Tell the NDIA about each listed event within 5 business days; aim for 3 (step 25)
  • Answer an NDIA notice by the date it sets (step 26)
  • Never enter a resident's home without lawful notice: 7 days for an inspection, 2 business days for a repair the resident asked for, or longer where the law says; no notice only in an emergency (step 18)
  • Inspect every dwelling with its residents every 6 months (step 19)
  • Sign a certification only when every matter has evidence (step 12)

docs.html:
1Purpose

The result: each who lives in one of our specialist disability accommodation (SDA) has a lawful, fair tenancy that they understand. A vacancy is filled with each 's say. The participant's providers have agreed in writing who does what. A is served only as the law allows, and the participant knows they can ask for a review.

This procedure gives effect to POL-SDA-05 Tenancy Management Policy (Specialist Disability Accommodation), C1 to C14.

the : a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the state or territory where the participant lives.

2When and who

Use this procedure for every dwelling [Provider name] has enrolled for SDA, and for every participant who lives in one.

It starts at six points:

  • a place becomes free, or is about to (steps 1 to 11)
  • a participant moves in, a starts or changes, or an is due for review (steps 12 to 14)
  • day to day: a , a , harm, a behaviour that may put a tenancy at risk, or an emergency (steps 15 to 21)
  • a participant's needs or circumstances change (steps 22 and 23)
  • we need to give a tenancy notice, or a tenancy ends (steps 24 to 28)
  • the register is due for review (steps 29 and 30).

A participant who already lives in a dwelling when you adopt this procedure starts at step 12.

Who acts:

  • The does the day-to-day tenancy work: advertising, applicants, residents, agreements, notices and records.
  • The decides who is offered a place, takes charge of every response to harm, and owns the register.
  • The Chief Executive reviews every notice that would end a tenancy and every decision that a home cannot meet a participant's needs.
  • The Quality Manager samples the register and reports to the governing body.
  • Every worker who sees, hears or is told of harm, a concern or a conflict passes it on. Workers include employees, contractors, agents and volunteers.
  • Each SIL provider acts as the arrangement says.

In a small provider one person may hold several roles. A sole trader holds them all. Where this procedure asks for a second person, the sole trader asks the for concerns, named in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register.

If [Provider name] also delivers SIL in the dwelling, we are both parties at step 12. Two different people sign. PRO-SDA-03 Conflict of Interest Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation) also applies.

In this procedure:

  • A business day is a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the state or territory where the participant lives.
  • "SDA Conditions Rule" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Specialist Disability Accommodation Conditions) Rule 2018.
  • "SDA Rules 2020" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Specialist Disability Accommodation) Rules 2020.
  • "Incident Rules" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Incident Management and Reportable Incidents) Rules 2018.
  • "Restrictive Practices Rules" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Restrictive Practices and Behaviour Support) Rules 2018.
  • The SDA Manager is the Service Manager for our SDA dwellings. The Tenancy Officer is the worker the SDA Manager assigns tenancy tasks to; in a small provider this is the SDA Manager.

3Before you start

  • Each dwelling is enrolled. It has a row in REG-SDA-01 SDA Dwelling Register with its design category, its building type and the number of residents it is enrolled for.
  • You can open each participant's FRM-RGT-01 Communication, Advocacy and Support Preferences Form. If it is more than 12 months old, update it with the participant before anything else.
  • You know whether each participant has agreed to share their information, and with whom. FRM-INF-01 Consent to Collect, Use and Share Information Form shows it.
  • In REG-SDA-02 SDA Tenancy and Vacancy Register, each kind of notice in [state or territory] has a notice rule row built from the dated list of laws in REG-QMS-03 Compliance Obligations Register. Each row was checked in the last 12 months and since the law last changed. If one is missing or old, do step 24 first.
  • You hold the urgent line number [urgent line number], the contact for SDA notices [NDIA contact], and the independent contact for concerns.
  • You hold STA-SDA-02 SDA Tenancy and Vacancies: Plain Summary, AGR-SDA-01 SDA Service Agreement and a blank AGR-SDA-02 SDA and Supported Independent Living Arrangements Agreement.

4Watch out

  • Call 000 first if anyone is hurt, in danger or threatened with a weapon. A delay can cost a life.
  • A late notice to the NDIA breaks a condition of enrolment. The NDIA can then cancel the dwelling's enrolment. It must first give at least 14 days to put it right (SDA Rules 2020, sections 27 and 29).
  • A tenancy never depends on a support choice. A notice given because a participant changed SIL provider, refused to sign an arrangement, complained or took a risk they chose is . It ends a home for the wrong reason.
  • A notice that breaks the state rule may be invalid. The participant is then unsure whether they must leave. We may also face a tribunal.
  • Locking, blocking access, taking belongings or limiting visitors is a . The Restrictive Practices Rules, section 6(e), call it environmental restraint. Without authorisation it can be a reportable incident.
  • Private details about an applicant told to a resident, or the reverse, breach privacy. Share only what each person agreed to.
  • A resident who feels unsafe cannot be talked round. Pushing a housemate on them can hurt them and ends their trust in us.
  • The person harmed keeps their home. Moving or limiting the person who was hurt punishes them for another person's act.
  • A concern about a manager can be buried if it goes only to that manager. Step 17 and If it goes wrong give another line.

5Steps

Fill a vacancy

Step 1

The Tenancy Officer

If a place in an becomes free, or will become free:

Declare the vacancy.

A place becomes free when a participant gives notice, is given notice, dies or moves out. Open a vacancy row. Write the date it arose, the dwelling, the room and the reason. Look up the dwelling in REG-SDA-01. Write its design category, its building type, the number of residents it is enrolled for and the number living there now. Tell the SDA Manager the same day. If a death caused the vacancy, read If it goes wrong first.

Result
The vacancy is on the record and the SDA Manager knows.
Record
REG-SDA-02 col AI
Time limit
Within 1 business day of learning of it (our standard)

Carries out: ←POL-SDA-05, commitment 3POL-SDA-05 C3Recorded in: →Register, Vacancy and declaringRegister col AI→Register, Record numberRegister col A

Step 2

Warning. A late notice breaks a condition of enrolment. The NDIA can then cancel the dwelling's enrolment.

The SDA Manager

If a vacancy arises, a participant gives notice or is given , we propose rent above the limit, or an emergency may make the dwelling unsuitable for SDA:

Notify the NDIA in writing.

Use the channel the NDIA currently asks to use. Write the dwelling, the event, the date it happened and, for a vacancy, that it is available to be filled. Keep a copy and the NDIA's reference. For rent above the limit, attach a certificate from a qualified property valuer that the rent is fair and reasonable. Work out the funding limit date for a dwelling enrolled for 2 to 5 residents. It applies when a participant dies, gives notice, or is given notice because of behaviour that might be a risk. The Rules then treat the participant as still living there until the vacancy is filled. That ends 60 days after the event for 2 or 3 residents, and 90 days for 4 or 5. Write that date. The NDIA decides how it affects payments. This step owns events (e) to (g) of Decision table 6 in PRO-SDA-01 Enrolment of SDA Properties Procedure, and uses that table for what to send. Events (a) to (d), such as a change of design category, belong to PRO-SDA-01 step 25. We aim to notify within 3 business days; the limit is 5.

Result
The NDIA has been told in writing, inside the limit, and the funding limit date is on the record.
Record
REG-SDA-02 col AJ; REG-SDA-02 col AK; REG-SDA-02 col BD; REG-SDA-02 col T; REG-SDA-02 col BN
Time limit
Within 5 business days of the event (statutory: SDA Rules 2020, section 29(2))

Carries out: ←POL-SDA-05, commitment 3POL-SDA-05 C3Recorded in: →Register, NDIA told of the vacancyRegister col AJ→Register, Funding limit dateRegister col AK→Register, NDIA told of the noticeRegister col BD→Register, Rent limit checkRegister col T→Register, Emergency continuityRegister col BN

Step 3

Warning. A vacancy shown only to people we already know shuts out people with the same need.

The Tenancy Officer

Advertise the vacancy.

Post a vacancy notice in at least 2 places that participants and support coordinators use. One must be open to the public without a login. Keep it open for at least 10 business days. State the suburb, the design category, the building type and the rooms. State the number of residents, with no personal detail. State the rent the participant would pay, how we choose using Decision table 1, the closing date, and how to ask for help to apply. Offer the notice in plain language, and in another format on request. Send it to each person on our list who may fit, and to each support coordinator who asked to hear of vacancies. Do not offer a gift, discount or reward to attract an applicant. While the notice is open, book the pre-move-in inspection, or the "vacant room and shared areas" check where the last full inspection is under 6 months old, under PRO-SDA-01 step 19, and ask each resident what matters to them in a housemate so steps 5 and 6 can run as applications arrive. Our target from step 1 to move-in is 30 business days, inside the 60-day funding limit. Law changing: from 20 November 2026 the NDIS Act 2013 bans inducements to provide supports (new section 73VA).

Result
Anyone who may fit can find the vacancy, in a form they can read, and knows how we choose.
Record
REG-SDA-02 col AL
Time limit
Within 5 business days of step 1 (our standard)

Carries out: ←POL-SDA-05, commitment 3POL-SDA-05 C3Recorded in: →Register, AdvertisingRegister col AL

Step 4

The Tenancy Officer

Help each applicant to apply.

Take an application in any form: phone, email, letter, in person or through a supporter. Give each applicant a number. Do not write their name in the register. Ask how they want us to communicate. Offer help to apply and an . Say how long the process takes, how we choose and when they will hear. Ask only what the criteria need. Get their consent on FRM-INF-01 before you ask anyone else about them.

Result
Every applicant has applied in a way they can, and knows how we choose and when they will hear.
Record
REG-SDA-02 col AM
Time limit
Acknowledge each application within 2 business days (our standard)

Carries out: ←POL-SDA-05, commitment 3POL-SDA-05 C3Recorded in: →Register, ApplicantsRegister col AM

Step 5

The SDA Manager

Check each applicant against Decision table 1.

Read the part of the applicant's plan that says they are eligible for SDA. Check the in it fit this dwelling. Check the applicant will have a private bedroom unless they freely choose to share. Count everyone who will live in the dwelling after the move. The count must not exceed the number it is enrolled for. Ask the applicant about their needs and wishes. With their consent, ask their support coordinator or SIL provider. Write the result for each criterion. Check for a of ours. Examples are a family or business tie, or a link between the vacancy and the applicant's choice of SIL provider. Declare it under PRO-SDA-03. Shortlist the applicants who meet criteria 1 and 2.

Result
Each applicant is checked on the same criteria and the SDA Manager has a shortlist.
Record
REG-SDA-02 col AN
Time limit
Within 5 business days of the closing date (our standard)

Carries out: ←POL-SDA-05, commitment 1POL-SDA-05 C1←POL-SDA-05, commitment 3POL-SDA-05 C3Recorded in: →Register, Applicant checks and criteriaRegister col AN

Step 6

Warning. A resident who is pushed to accept a housemate may stop raising concerns.

The Tenancy Officer

If the dwelling has other residents:

Ask each resident how they feel about a new person moving in.

Ask before any offer. Ask about the criteria while the vacancy is advertised (step 3) and about the shortlist here, so the two conversations run inside the advertising period. Ask each resident alone, in their own way of communicating, with a supporter or advocate if they want one. Say a place is free and a person may move in. Tell them only what the shortlisted applicants agreed to share. Ask what matters to them in a housemate and what they would like to know. Ask whether they want to meet the person and whether they have any worry. Say that their answer will be heard and never affects their tenancy. For a resident who does not use words, watch and ask a supporter who knows them. The SIL provider may already hold FRM-SIL-06 Co- Consultation and Matching Record for this vacancy. If so, ask for it with the resident's consent. Do not ask the same questions twice. Write each answer in a few words, without names. Use Decision table 2.

Result
Every resident has been heard before anyone is offered the place.
Record
REG-SDA-02 col AO
Time limit
Give each resident at least 5 business days to answer, unless they answer sooner (our standard)

Carries out: ←POL-SDA-05, commitment 3POL-SDA-05 C3Recorded in: →Register, Residents askedRegister col AO

Step 7

The SDA Manager

If a resident says they are worried, do not feel safe, or do not want the person:

Meet the resident to find a way through.

Meet them alone, with an independent advocate or supporter if they want one. Ask what would make it work, such as meeting the person first or a trial visit. Use Decision table 2. Tell them nothing private about the applicant. Do not press them to agree. If they say they do not feel safe, do not offer the place to that applicant until they say the worry is settled. If it is not settled, offer the place to the next applicant and ask each resident again. Sometimes the worry is about who the applicant is, not how they would live together. Explain that we cannot refuse an applicant for that reason. Ask what worries them in daily life.

Result
Each worry has been heard and worked through, and nobody is pushed into a housemate they feel unsafe with.
Record
REG-SDA-02 col AP
Time limit
Meet within 2 business days of the resident's answer (our standard)

Carries out: ←POL-SDA-05, commitment 3POL-SDA-05 C3Recorded in: →Register, Resident's worryRegister col AP

Step 8

The SDA Manager

Decide which applicant to offer the place to.

Use only the criteria in Decision table 1 and what each resident said. Choose between applicants who meet criteria 1 and 2 by the applicant's own wishes and the residents' views. Use the date they applied only to separate applicants who are equal. Write the reasons against each criterion, in plain words an applicant could test. If no applicant meets criteria 1 and 2, or a resident's safety worry is unresolved for every applicant, offer the place to nobody. Keep the vacancy open and go back to step 3. If the SDA Manager has a conflict of interest, the Chief Executive decides.

Result
The place is offered on stated reasons, with every resident's view taken into account.
Record
REG-SDA-02 col AQ
Time limit
Within 5 business days of the last resident's answer (our standard)

Carries out: ←POL-SDA-05, commitment 3POL-SDA-05 C3Recorded in: →Register, Decision and reasonsRegister col AQ

Step 9

The Tenancy Officer

Offer the place to the chosen applicant.

Offer in the applicant's way of communicating. Give them time to decide. Offer a visit to the dwelling, and a meeting with any resident who agrees. Give them the draft SDA service agreement (AGR-SDA-01), the rent they would pay, a draft AGR-SDA-02 and STA-SDA-02. Go through each in their way. Ask them to say back what it means. Offer an independent advocate and independent advice about the agreement. Say that the offer never depends on who delivers their . Say that they can ask for this process in any format. If they decline, say that it counts for nothing against them. Then go back to step 8 and offer the place to the next applicant.

Result
The applicant chooses freely, with what they need to know in a form they understand.
Record
REG-SDA-02 col AR
Time limit
At least 5 business days to decide, and longer if they ask (our standard)

Carries out: ←POL-SDA-05, commitment 3POL-SDA-05 C3←POL-SDA-05, commitment 4POL-SDA-05 C4Recorded in: →Register, Offer and the applicant's choiceRegister col AR

Step 10

The Tenancy Officer

Tell each applicant who was not offered the place.

Say the result, and the reasons against each criterion, in plain words and in their way. Share nothing about any other applicant or resident. Tell them how to ask the Chief Executive for another look and how to complain to us. Give them the 's number, 1800 035 544. Offer an advocate. Keep them on our list for the next vacancy if they agree.

Result
Each applicant knows why, and how to challenge the decision.
Record
REG-SDA-02 col AS
Time limit
Within 5 business days of the chosen applicant's answer (our standard)

Carries out: ←POL-SDA-05, commitment 3POL-SDA-05 C3Recorded in: →Register, Others toldRegister col AS

Step 11

The SDA Manager

Confirm the move-in checks.

Obtain the limits check row number from PRO-SDA-01 step 16, dated within 30 days. It shows the dwelling is enrolled, the numbers and the are met, and the room, bathroom and plan fit. Do not confirm the move-in without it. Check that the SDA service agreement is signed. If not, check that a proposed copy was given and explained, and that we will provide SDA on its terms. Carries out: ←POL-SDA-05, commitment 14POL-SDA-05 C14Recorded in: →Register, Review findingsRegister col BO

6Decision

Decision table 1: how we choose (steps 3, 5 and 8). Every applicant is checked on the same criteria.

No.CriterionWhat we checkHow it counts
1SDA funding and fitThe applicant's plan includes SDA funding. The dwelling has the design category and building type in their plan, or the NDIA has agreed in writing that this dwelling can be funded for them. The place is a private bedroom unless they freely choose to share. The residents after the move do not exceed the enrolled numberMust be met

4The residents' viewsWhat each resident said about living with a new person. A worry about safety is settled under Decision table 2Weighs in favour

Decision table 2: what the resident says (steps 6 and 7).

The resident saysThen

They do not feel safe with the personDo not offer the place to that applicant until the resident says the worry is settled. Meet them at step 7. Offer the next applicant if it is not settled

Explain that we cannot refuse an applicant for that reason. Ask what worries them in daily life. Offer an advocate. Do not let that view decide the matter
They cannot say, or do not answerAsk again within 5 business days, in another way or through a supporter who knows them. If there is still no answer, record that and go on. Never treat silence as agreement

Decision table 3: what the person raises (step 15).

What the person raisesTreat it asWhat we do

With consent, ask the SIL provider and the behaviour support practitioner whether a disability-related need is behind it and whether a reasonable adjustment or a plan review could meet it; no notice relying on behaviour starts until they have answered. 7If it goes wrong

IfThen
A participant refuses to take part in the consultation, the arrangement or a hearingRespect it and record their words. Their tenancy and supports do not change. Offer again once within 28 days, with a different person, time or place, or through an advocate. After two refusals, record their standing answer and ask again only at the 12-month review or when things change. With consent, ask people who know them well
A SIL provider will not sign, or does not answer within 10 business daysRecord the reason or the silence at step 13. Offer again every 28 days. Tell the participant plainly. Their tenancy and supports continue. Tell the Chief Executive after 2 attempts without an answer
Nobody is sure who decides for a participant, or family and the participant disagreeDo not go on the family's word. The SDA Manager reads any order or instrument and records what it covers. The participant still takes part, and an advocate is offered

The vacancy follows a deathDo steps 1 and 2 at once, because the limits run. Speak with the family or the person the participant named, and tell the housemates yourself, in their way, before the notice goes up. The Quality Manager, as the authorised notifier, tells the NDIS Commission under PRO-INC-02

The 5 business day limit to the NDIA cannot be extended: notify late rather than never, tell the Chief Executive the same day, and enter it in REG-QMS-01
The Tenancy Officer or SDA Manager is awayThe delegate named in REG-GOV-01 acts. A statutory time limit never waits for a return
The concern is about the SDA Manager, or another managerTake it to the Chief Executive. If it is about the Chief Executive or a sole trader, take it to the independent contact for concerns. You can always phone the NDIS Commission on 1800 035 544. A person never decides, approves or closes a matter about themselves

A notice was served late, to the wrong person or in the wrong formTell the Chief Executive the same day. Do not rely on it. Tell the participant in plain words, withdraw it in writing, and serve it again correctly if it is still needed. Record it in column BE
A participant says they fear losing their home for raising somethingTell the Chief Executive the same day. Treat any threat to their home as an incident under PRO-INC-01. Offer an advocate
A SIL provider stops supporting a participant suddenlyAsk the participant what they want. With consent, tell their support coordinator the same day. Their home is unchanged. Open a new arrangement row when a new provider starts
Personal information is shared without consent, or sent to the wrong personTell the SDA Manager the same day. Start PRO-INF-02 Privacy and Data Breach Response Procedure
The participant's needs exceed the dwelling's design category or functionality, and no modification can workGo to step 23. Tell the NDIA at step 2 if the design category or suitability changes
An arrangement is out of date, or a contact named in it has leftReview it within 10 business days at step 12. Until then the SDA Manager is our contact. Ask each SIL provider for its new contact the same day
An applicant or a resident says the process was unfairTreat it as a complaint under PRO-FBK-01. The Chief Executive gives another look within 10 business days. Never let it count against them
The system is downUse paper. Phone calls and statutory time limits still apply. Enter the rows within 2 business days of the system coming back

8Done means

A vacancy is finished when all of these are true:

  • the NDIA was told in writing within 5 business days of the event
  • every resident was asked before any offer, and each worry was settled, or the place was not offered to that applicant
  • the place was offered on stated reasons, and every other applicant was told the result and how to challenge it
  • the move-in checks were confirmed, and the place is filled or a new advertising round is open.

An arrangement is finished when all of these are true:

  • each matter has a party responsible, a role, a contact and a response time
  • each party's decision is recorded, in the participant's words for the participant
  • each party has a copy, and the next review date is set.

A change in a participant's needs is finished when all of these are true:

  • the participant was told the outcome in their way
  • the providers they chose were told, within 2 business days of their agreement
  • where the home cannot meet their needs, the participant has been offered help to find another home.

A concern, conflict or harm is finished when all of these are true:

  • the person has been told the outcome in their way
  • the dwelling is safe
  • any change to prevent a repeat is in REG-QMS-01.
  • the concern row shows it was acknowledged within 1 business day and answered within 5

A notice is finished when all of these are true:

  • the rule was checked, and the Chief Executive approved any notice that ends a tenancy
  • the participant was heard, where step 25 applies
  • the notice was served as the law requires
  • the participant was told how to seek a review
  • the NDIA was told, where it had to be.

These records now exist:

  • a row in REG-SDA-02 for each tenancy, arrangement, vacancy, notice, change, home event and concern, and its review rows
  • AGR-SDA-02 for each participant who has a SIL provider
  • the incident report (FRM-INC-01), complaint or repair that any concern led to, linked in column O
  • a dated review row for every weekly, monthly and 3-monthly review.

9Quick card

158 words
  • Call 000 if anyone is hurt or in danger, then phone the SDA Manager or the urgent line (step 17)
  • Tell the NDIA in writing within 5 business days of a vacancy or a notice (step 2)
  • Ask every resident before any offer, and never offer over a resident's safety worry (step 6)
  • Never give notice because of a support choice, a complaint or a refusal to sign (step 24)
  • Check the state rule before every notice, and get the Chief Executive's approval before a notice ends a tenancy (step 24)
  • Hear the participant before you decide anything that ends or limits a tenancy (step 25)
  • Tell the participant how to seek a review with every notice (step 27)
  • Acknowledge a concern about the dwelling within 1 business day; make an emergency one safe the same day and an urgent one within 24 hours (step 15)
  • Never lock, block access or take belongings because of behaviour (step 20)

docs.html:
1What this agreement is for

This agreement sets out how a , their specialist disability accommodation (SDA) provider and each of their providers will work together. Its aim is that the participant's home works for them and for the people they live with.

In this agreement "you" is the participant. "We" is [Provider name], the , who owns or manages the . A "" is any other NDIS provider that delivers supported independent living supports to you in the dwelling.

It is one agreement with one copy for each party. A SIL provider can attach it to its own service agreement with you, and we can attach it to your SDA service agreement. Neither attachment changes either of those agreements. Nothing here limits your rights under your or the NDIS rules.

Complete it when you move in, when you get a new SIL provider, when something in it changes and at least every 12 months. The completes Sections A and B with you first, and then takes the same draft to each SIL provider. Where [Provider name] also provides your SIL, the signs for the home and the Service Manager signs for the supports; a sole trader signs once and the for named in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register countersigns.

This agreement authorises no and no limit on your visitors, belongings or movement.

2Terms

T1

This agreement is separate from your SDA service agreement and from each service agreement you hold with a SIL provider. None of them depends on another. Each time in these Terms is our standard, and Section B of the Schedule can set a shorter time. A is a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the state or territory where you live. "Provider party" means us and each SIL provider; the duties in these Terms that say "each provider party" are theirs, not yours.

Answers: ←Legislation, indicator (3)Legislation (3)

T2

You keep your home whatever you decide about your supports. Changing SIL provider, not signing this agreement, making a complaint or taking a risk you have chosen never puts your tenancy at risk.

T3

You can change your SIL provider, in whole or in part, at any time. A new SIL provider takes over its part of this agreement by signing it. We and your old SIL provider will help you change without disrupting your home.

T4

Section B of the Schedule gives each matter a party responsible, a role, a contact person and a response time. Those are the rights and responsibilities of each party for that matter. The party named does the work. Nobody leaves a matter undone because another party is also involved.

Answers: ←Legislation, indicator (3)Legislation (3)←Legislation, indicator (3)(a)Legislation (3)(a)

T5

We are responsible for the dwelling and your tenancy unless Section B says otherwise. That covers repairs and upkeep, safety equipment, house rules, vacancies and . Each SIL provider is responsible for the supports it delivers.

T6

Each provider party names a contact person, who answers the other parties within the response time in Section B. The provider parties tell each other early about anything that affects the shared home. We tell each SIL provider in writing of any change to our dwelling policies or house rules within 10 business days. They share your personal information only as Term 16 allows.

Answers: ←Legislation, indicator (3)(a)Legislation (3)(a)

T7

Anyone can raise a concern about the dwelling with any party. A provider party who hears one passes it to us the same day. We acknowledge it within 1 business day of the day you first raised it. We give you an answer, or a date for one, within 5 business days. We make an urgent safety problem safe within 24 hours, and the same day where your safety or a life-support device depends on it. We tell you the outcome in your way of communicating. Nobody is treated worse for raising a concern.

Answers: ←Legislation, indicator (3)(d)Legislation (3)(d)

T8

When people who live in the home are in , each party helps early and fairly. We meet each person affected, alone, within 5 business days of learning of it. They can have an advocate. We use mediation only if everyone agrees and nobody is afraid. A disagreement that is only about a SIL provider's supports stays with that provider. Nobody is moved, or has their access limited, to settle a conflict.

Answers: ←Legislation, indicator (3)(b)Legislation (3)(b)

T9

If violence, abuse, neglect, exploitation or discrimination happens or is alleged, each provider party acts at once. Anyone in danger gets a call to 000 first. Each provider party reports as the NDIS Incident Rules require for its own supports; question 9 says who notifies the , whether both providers must, who leads the investigation, who tells you and the people you choose, and how the providers share findings with your consent. For us, our Quality Manager decides whether an incident is reportable and notifies the NDIS Commission within 24 hours of becoming aware where it involves death, serious injury, abuse or neglect, unlawful sexual or physical contact or sexual misconduct, or an unauthorised restrictive practice that resulted in harm, and otherwise within 5 business days. A provider party who learns of it tells the other provider parties: the same day if the dwelling is unsafe or damaged, and within 1 business day in any other case. We support each person affected. The person harmed keeps their home. You have no reporting duty under this term.

Answers: ←Legislation, indicator (3)(c)Legislation (3)(c)←Legislation, indicator (4)Legislation (4)

T10

Section B says whether matter for you. Where they do, your behaviour support plan stays with the people who write it and carry it out; we do not hold or act on its content. We take no about behaviour until we have spoken with you and offered you an advocate. We also ask your behaviour support practitioner and SIL provider, with your agreement, what would help. If we are ever asked to apply a lock, camera, gate or visitor limit, we would be an implementing provider and would need the state or territory authorisation and the NDIS Commission reporting the law requires; a SIL provider's request alone never allows it.

Answers: ←Legislation, indicator (3)(e)Legislation (3)(e)

T11

A change in your circumstances or supports is agreed with you before it is passed on. A provider party who learns of a change tells the other parties you have chosen within 2 business days; you may tell anyone, or no one. If you need a change to the dwelling, we decide it under FRM-SDA-01 Dwelling and Adjustment Request, after asking each other affected. If the dwelling can no longer meet your needs, we tell you first, in person, within 2 business days of confirming it. We then help you look for another home.

Answers: ←Legislation, indicator (3)(f)Legislation (3)(f)←Legislation, indicator (5)Legislation (5)

T12

When a place in your dwelling is free, we ask you and each housemate how you feel about a new person. We ask before we offer the place. We take your needs, wishes, choices and situation into account. We do not offer the place to a person you do not feel safe living with until your worry is settled. Your SIL provider helps you take part if you ask.

Answers: ←Legislation, indicator (3)(h)Legislation (3)(h)

T13

Section B sets out how supports and accommodation continue in an emergency or a disaster. We give each SIL provider the dwelling's emergency information before its first shift. If the dwelling cannot be used, we tell you the same day what we are doing and who is helping. We work with your SIL provider and the to find you a temporary place that meets your needs as soon as possible, and within 24 hours. We keep your tenancy, and you pay no rent for any time you cannot live in the dwelling.

Answers: ←Legislation, indicator (3)(g)Legislation (3)(g)

T14

You can have visitors in your home, including overnight, as you choose. Any rule about visitors is made with you and your housemates. A limit on your visitors, belongings or movement exists only if an authorised behaviour support plan says so. If a visitor puts someone at risk, we act under Term 9. We do not ban a visitor on our own authority.

T15

The workers of each SIL provider may enter the dwelling to deliver the supports you chose. We do not restrict that access. You decide who enters your bedroom, except where the law allows entry. We give you notice before we enter, as your SDA service agreement says: at least 7 days for an inspection and at least 2 business days for a repair you asked for, or longer where the law requires, and none only in an emergency.

Answers: ←Legislation, indicator (1)Legislation (1)

T16

We share your information between the parties only as you agree in Question 3. You can change what you agree at any time. We share without your agreement only when the law requires it, or to prevent serious harm.

T17

We explain this agreement in the language, mode of communication and terms you are most likely to understand. You can have an advocate, a supporter, independent advice and time to think. You can say no. If you do not agree or do not sign, we record it in your words. Nothing changes in your tenancy or your supports, and we offer again within 20 business days. Each party gets a copy, and yours is in the format you prefer.

Answers: ←Legislation, indicator (3)Legislation (3)←Legislation, indicator (9)Legislation (9)

T18

We review this agreement with you at least every 12 months, when you ask, when a party asks and when your SIL provider changes. A change needs your agreement. This agreement ends for a SIL provider when it stops supporting you in the dwelling. It stays in place for the other parties.

T19

If you are unhappy with anything in this agreement, tell any party. A concern about us goes through our complaints system. You can also contact the NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commission on 1800 035 544. You can ask an for help. You can go to the tribunal or court that hears tenancy disputes in [state or territory].

What each SIL provider agrees

By signing, each SIL provider agrees, for itself, to: do the work Section B names it for, within the response times written there; tell us the same day of anything that makes the dwelling unsafe or damaged, and within 1 business day of any other incident that affects the shared home; tell the other parties you have chosen of a change in your circumstances or supports within 2 business days, after you have agreed; report incidents in connection with its own supports as the NDIS Incident Rules require, and follow what question 9 says about who notifies, who leads and who tells you; name its nominated person for the safety walk-through before its first shift, brief its own workers, and tell us which of its workers hold keys or codes (question 18); respect your privacy and share your information only as question 3 allows; and place no condition on your tenancy and never ask us to limit your access, visitors or belongings. These are the SIL provider's duties under this agreement. You have none of them.

+Privacy

This part is not one the anatomy names for this kind of document.

We collect the information in this agreement to set up the between you, us and your SIL providers, and to meet the SDA Conditions Rule, section 10, and the NDIS Practice Standards.

Each party holds a copy. Ours is read by the Tenancy Officer, the SDA Manager and the Chief Executive; each SIL provider's copy is read by the people it names in Section B. In REG-SDA-02 we write your participant number, never your name. An auditor or the NDIS Commission may see it as the law allows. The parties share your personal information only as question 3 allows.

You can see any party's copy and ask for it to be corrected; ask any worker. Asking never puts your home or your supports at risk. Each party keeps its copy for 7 years after this agreement ends for it (NDIS Act 2013, section 45B). POL-INF-01 Information Management Policy sets how we store and protect ours.

form.intro:
Use this form each time a participant wants something about their specialist disability accommodation dwelling changed. It follows one request from the day it is made to the day the participant says the change works.

A modification is a change to the building, or to something fixed to it. An adjustment is a change to how we manage the dwelling, give notice, enter the home or communicate. A request about who visits or lives in the dwelling is recorded here too.

Who completes it: the worker who hears the request starts Section A the same day. The completes Section B. The completes Sections C to F. The participant never has to fill in a form to be heard.

Start a form when:

  • a participant asks, in words, signs, pictures or behaviour
  • a supporter or another provider asks, and the participant agrees
  • a worker sees a need, or a need comes up at a dwelling check or the yearly rights check
  • a participant's needs or circumstances change.

Have ready: the participant's FRM-RGT-01 Communication, Advocacy and Support Preferences Form, and the dwelling's row in REG-SDA-01 SDA Dwelling Register.

A simple adjustment can be agreed on the day. It costs nothing, changes no building or fixture, affects no other resident and breaks no law. For one, complete Sections A and B, then question 24 (write "agreed on the day"), question 28 (the date and how the participant was told) and questions 35 to 37. Skip every other question. The form is for modifications, and for any request that is refused, approved in part or affects another resident.

What happens next: the participant is told the decision within 20 business days of the request. PRO-SDA-02 Rights and Responsibilities Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation) sets every step.

A repair is not a request under this form. Report a repair under PRO-SDA-01 Enrolment of SDA Properties Procedure. This form never ends a tenancy and authorises no .

When to use which questions:

  • Adjustment agreed on the day: Sections A and B; question 24; question 28; questions 35 to 37.
  • Modification, or an adjustment that needs assessment: every question in Sections A to F.
  • Request refused, approved in part, or affecting a shared area or another resident: every question in Sections A to F, including Section D and the review at question 26.
  • Request the dwelling cannot meet: every question, and question 31.
  • An adjustment agreed on the day is also written as a one-line modification record in REG-SDA-01 (request number, date, participant, what was agreed, date told, records updated).
form.privacy:
We collect this information to decide the request and to make the change safely. The SDA Manager, the Tenancy Officer, the Chief Executive and the Quality Manager see it. An adviser or contractor sees only what they need, and only with the participant's consent. An auditor sees it only to check our work.

The participant does not have to give a diagnosis. We ask what the change needs to do, not why the participant's body or mind works as it does. We never ask a participant to explain a wish for privacy, a visitor or a relationship.

We keep the form on the participant's file. We write no other resident's name or personal details on it. Each resident's view is kept on that resident's own file.

The participant can see this form and ask us to correct it. They use FRM-INF-02 Request to Access or Correct Personal Information Form, or they ask any worker. Asking for a change never puts a participant's home at risk.
form.after:
• Worker: give Section A to the Tenancy Officer the day the request is made. The Tenancy Officer enters it in REG-SDA-01 and gets the request number the same day (our standard).
  • SDA Manager: put an interim in place the same day where question 9 is yes (our standard).
  • Tenancy Officer: complete Section B and acknowledge the request within 2 business days of question 2 (our standard).
  • SDA Manager: ask the dwelling's owner in writing within 5 business days of question 2, where question 18 needs it (our standard).
  • SDA Manager: decide within 15 business days of question 2 (our standard). Send "approved in part", "not approved" and "the need cannot be met in this dwelling" to the Chief Executive first. The Chief Executive reviews within 3 business days (our standard).
  • Tenancy Officer: explain the decision within 2 business days of it being final, and within 20 business days of question 2 (our standard).
  • SDA Manager: notify the NDIA within 5 business days of the event where question 20 is not "none" (statutory: SDA Rules 2020, section 29(2)).
  • If the request is about the SDA Manager's own conduct, give the form to the Chief Executive. If it is about the Chief Executive or a sole trader, give it to the independent contact named in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register.
